title: DRAKE Caterpillar - Preparing to Enter Service
Monthly Studio Report: November 2016
digest:
- Greetings Citizens!: November 2016 was one for the record books!
- Engineering: With the push for 2.6, the team made huge progress on the vehicle system and flight control, while laying the groundwork for further development of the item system.
- Tech Design: Our tech design team continues to plug away supporting the engineers in their endeavor to get Item2.0 up and out the door.
- Art: The Art Teams have been dividing their efforts between Star Marine, Squadron 42 and the Persistent Universe.
- Tech Content: The team was intensely focused on cleaning up the animation streaming system and unified the character head assets.
- Narrative: In the wake of last month’s motion capture shoot, the team worked with the editor to review the footage to put together selected footage for Chris to review.
- Quality Assurance: LAQA’s primary focus was on supporting local developers, and providing QA support and participating in the November Live Stream event.
- Cloud Imperium Austin: November has been a big month for Star Citizen.
- Design: The Austin Design Team has been looking ahead to 3.0.0. for the majority of November.
- Art: Ship artists Chris Smith and Josh Coons are chugging away on their respective ships.
- Animation: The PU Animation Team has been supporting Squadron 42 by implementing animations for the various Usables that have been set up in the Idris by Design.
- Backend Services: The Backend Team spent the month delving into various areas of the project.
- Quality Assurance: The first half of the month testing focused on Star Marine and Arena Commander to ensure they were ready for the November Live Stream.
- Player Relations: If Player Relations is unfamiliar to you, it’s because it’s just been created!
- IT/Operations: Network Services Manager Paul Vaden and IT Director Mike Jones spent time in LA with IT Manager Dennis Daniel in order to prepare for the November Live Stream event.
- LiveOps/DevOps: 2.6 was a huge focus this month as we prepare all our servers and publishing systems for Star Marine.
- Art: The big focus this month had to be the Prowler.
- VFX: This month, the VFX team finished a full pass on two of the new ships going into 2.6 including the 85X and the Caterpillar.
- Design: Most of the S42 designers have been working out of our Frankfurt office throughout November in an effort to work as efficiently as possible with the system designers that are helping with the…
- Audio: This month the Audio department, like the rest of the team, was pretty heavily focused on Star Marine and other 2.6 needs.
- UI: Since last month, the UI team has been continuing work on the implementation of the new front-end menus and Electronic Access lobbies.
- Programming: Again working hard on all the features and polish for 2.6 and on the FPS for the Star Marine games.
- Graphics: The depth of field effect is getting a complete overhaul to vastly improve its speed (up to 10x faster in some cases).
- Animation: We have been mostly supporting the upcoming Star Marine release.
- Quality Assurance: To help with 2.6.0 feature testing and preparation for the live stream, we split our team into three groups, with Liam leading the Squadron 42 testing, Mike leading Arena Commander and Crusader…
- Cinematics: For the SQ42 campaign we’re continuing work on video comms and several conversational scenes, cleaning and editing the required animations as well as setting up and lighting them.
- VFX: During the past month, the Frankfurt VFX work has been focused on polishing effects for the 2.6 release.
- Quality Assurance: DEQA’s main focus for November was Star Marine, Squadron 42, as well as testing new engine-side features.
- Environmental Art: This month the DE Environment team grew by a few people, so the senior staff spent time getting them acquainted to our internal processes.
- Tech Art: Like many other departments, Tech Art spent the month supporting 2.6 as well as S42.

title: Q&A: Drake Kraken
digest:
Following the launch of the Kraken from Drake Interplanetary, we took your community-voted questions to our designers to give you more information on the recently unveiled capital ship. Special thanks to John Crewe and Todd Papy for answering these questions.
- Do the Kraken’s shields cover other ships parked on the deck?: The Kraken’s shields cover the hull of the ship and do not cover the ships or people that may be on the exposed landing pads.
- What are the Kraken’s refuel, restock, and repair abilities for docked ships?: The Kraken is, in many ways, a mobile base.
- Can you quantum travel while ships are parked on the deck? What about with people on the deck?: Yes, you’ll be able to Quantum with ships parked on the deck.
- What are your plans for landing on the Kraken while it is in motion?: Like the Idris or other ships where you can land whilst they are in motion, we’ll provide automated landing solutions for those who do not wish to attempt a manual landing.
- Can you spawn ships from the Kraken?: When you spawn your Kraken, you will be able to spawn ships in/on it if you own them, but beyond that point no other ships can be spawned dynamically on-board.
- What happens to the landed/hangar-landed ships if the Kraken pilot logs off/is disconnected? And what will happen when the owners of the landed ships log off? Do their ships persist until the Kraken is despawned, or is the pad free for another one to land on?: The Kraken will follow the same rule-set as the persistent bed log off system we current have in game, if the owner of the Kraken logs off and there are no other players on-board, then it will be…
- How does the Kraken’s armor compare to other ships in its size-class, like the Idris?: In true Drake fashion, the approach to construction prizes pragmatism and cost-effectiveness.
- What is meant by “Towards the rear of the ship public accommodations can be found for visitors and associates?” Does the Kraken offer any special function or gameplay for public services like shops, bars, medical, or trading for those who are waiting for repair or just visiting?: There are onboard accommodation rooms to cover 1-2 players per landing pad.
- With the Kraken being capital ship size will it have escape pods now unlike other Drake ships?: Drake sees no need to provide expensive escape pods when the Kraken can hold plenty of ships to facilitate escape in the “unlikely” event of an emergency.
- How many ships can the Kraken hold and still quantum drive with?: The current design for Quantum Travel requires all the doors to be shut before the Quantum Drive can be initiated, with no requirements beyond that, such as checking for maximum ship amounts.
- Can the Kraken equip military grade items or only civilian/industrial?: The Kraken can only equip Civilian and Industrial items and comes with Civilian Grade C items by default.
- The Kraken brochure talks about configuring the rear hangars to fit our needs. Does this mean that the Kraken might have some modular capabilities to outfit those hangars to suit other functions like extended medical/S&R or salvage processing?: Drake always look to maximize the use of their spaceships, and whilst these rear cargo holds are ostensibly for cargo, there is a significant amount of real estate that could be re-purposed in the…
- How will this ship defend against armed boarding parties or other guests who refuse to leave?: The internal layout of the ship provides quite a few choke-points from the landing pads, allowing a somewhat organized defense against boarding.
- Can we transfer cargo between docked/landed ships? If not, can cargo be transferred between docked/landed ships and the Kraken?: Every external landing pad has access to the internal tram route via a loading hatch located within the airlock antechamber.
- The Kraken shows some concept of it landed in a desert, as well as parked at Lorville . How can we expect it to fare in atmospheric flight. Does it have VTOL?: As with all ships of this size, the atmospheric flight performance can be characterized as poor at best, but the Kraken does have multiple VTOL thrusters to allow it to take off and land in…

title: Inside Star Citizen - Friends in Low Places
Star Citizen Monthly Report: January 2020
digest:
- AI: We start January’s report with Combat AI, who improved the cover generation and NPC cover-use mentioned last month.
- Art (Environment): Environment Art kicked off the year in earnest, finalizing microTech’s moons and updating their geology assets.
- Art (Ships): In the US, Ship Art finalized art for the upcoming Esperia Prowler.
- Art (Weapons): January saw the FPS Weapons Team kicking off two new weapons – the Lightning Bolt Co.’s Atzkav sniper rifle and Yubarev pistol.
- Audio: Audio started off January by spending time scheduling for the quarter.
- Backend Services: Backend Engineering spent early January planning and scheduling for the next quarter’s development.
- Characters: The Character Team spent most of the month working on assets for the PU.
- Community: The Community Team kicked off 2020 with the Red Festival.
- Design: Alongside planning and bug fixing, last month saw Design setting up the new shops coming in Alpha 3.9.
- Engineering: January saw the Engineering Team continue with physics threading and performance improvements.
- Features (Gameplay): With the quarterly plans locked, the team provided engineering support for the upcoming prison mission feature.
- Features (Vehicles): The US-based Feature Team began improving radar and ping detection, including simplifying entity detection, reworking the A/R marker display, and allowing low-signature entities.
- Graphics: With the bulk of Planet Tech v4 complete, the Graphics Team began looking into improvements to the organic shader to enable it to take advantage of physical-based shading.
- Level Design: Level Design’s January started with location planning, identifying dependencies, and organizing schedules.
- Lighting: Last month, the Lighting Team tackled several bugs and polish tasks that had been put on the backburner while release work was prioritized.
- Player Relations: In addition to supporting various promotions and events, Player Relations worked to stabilize the incremental Alpha 3.8 patches, with focus currently on Alpha 3.8.2.
- Props: The Props Team started the year off cleaning up bugs and taking stock of materials and textures in the ongoing process of improving asset quality.
- QA: Development-wise, QA tested the key elements of the incremental Alpha 3.8 patches, including the Drake Cutlass Red and Anvil Carrack.
- System Design: System Design spent time in January finishing mining consumables.
- Tech Animation: Tech Animation fixed several small bugs in the animation pipeline and reworked the PlayBlast animation tool in Maya to improve efficiency.
- Tech Art: Tech Art continued to flesh out the runtime Rig Logic tools for Maya.
- Turbulent: Turbulent supported the release of the Cutlass Red, working with in-house teams to build the web page and manage the backend.
- User Interface (UI): Much of the UI Art Team’s January focus was on hi-tech environmental screens for New Babbage and developing the visual style of the prison UI screens, which have a more retro-inspired functional look.
- VFX: The VFX Team further improved Planet Tech v4, specifically wind strength values across each location.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: August 2026
summary: Welcome to August’s PU Monthly Report! While most teams contributed toward Alpha 4.10: Siege of Orison throughout the month, many devs continued with tasks for exciting content coming soon and further down the road. Read on for all the latest details.
digest:
Welcome to August’s PU Monthly Report! While most teams contributed toward Alpha 4.10: Siege of Orison throughout the month, many devs continued with tasks for exciting content coming soon and further down the road. Read on for all the latest details.
- AI Content: The recent Alpha 4.10 patch marked an exciting milestone for AI Content, with the re-release of Recco Battaglia and the introduction of a narrative-driven mission chain.
- AI (Features & Tech): AI Features and Tech spent August improving Starchitect, fixing nav-meshes, and progressing with Star Paws.
- Animation: Last month, animations were worked on for the apex valakkar, including for major attacks on ship targets.
- Art (Characters): In August, the Character Art team finalized a new combat armor set and its variants, completed Subscriber flair items, and progressed with a new type of armor.
- Art (Ships): The UK team began the month with a final polish pass on the Kruger Stingray after utilizing the PTU to catch a number of small bugs before its full release.
- Community: August began with the team supporting two ongoing events that started in July: Foundation Festival, which welcomes new pilots and celebrates the community members who help them find their way, and…
- Narrative: Work continued in August on generating mission text for the huge number of missions that will be arriving with Nyx I.
- Online Technology: Last month, the Online Services team focused on improving the reliability of missions and contracts, specifically the system that generates jobs and delivery tasks.
- R&D: August saw the R&D team working on planet atmosphere, including making improvements to the overcast skylight.
- Tech Art/Animation: Throughout August, the Technical Animation team focused on the systems that make characters look and move convincingly, including faces, deformation, cloth, and creatures.
